sources.citation: Goudswaard, Nelleke. 2005. The Begak (Ida'an) Language of Sabah. LOT Dissertation Series 107. Utrecht: LOT. xix+520 pp.
sources.quote: 'All words receive final stress. Stress is expressed by pitch, length and loudness. Syllable weight does not play a role in stress assignment. Although stress is not rhythmic or recurrent in Begak, the iamb will be adopted as foot structure for the language.' Ch.1: 'Stress in the Ida'an language is word-final'. Sec. 3.2.4: phonological word 'is minimally bisyllabic and has final stress'; monosyllabic function words 'are nevertheless stressed'.

sources.citation: Moody, David C. 1993. 'Ida'an phonemics'. In Michael E. Boutin & Inka Pekkanen (eds.), Phonological descriptions of Sabah languages: studies from ten languages, 131-146. Sabah Museum Monograph 4. Kota Kinabalu: Sabah Museum.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: p. 131 (sec. 2 Phonemes, opening): "There are twenty-two segmental phonemes in Ida'an: sixteen consonants /p t k ? b d g s d3 m n ng l r w y/ and six vowels /i u e a o schwa/. Stress is contrastive." p. 134: "I posit the secondary vowel phoneme /o/ to account for the occurrence of penultimate [o]. Ultimate [o], which is always stressed, and [schwa], which is always unstressed, are allophones of /schwa/." p. 135 (vowel allophone list): "/schwa/ [schwa] lower-mid central slightly rounded vowel; occurs in non-final unstressed syllables: /pen'dan/ 'not yet' ... [o] mid back rounded vowel; occurs in final stressed syllables: /e?/ [o?] 'yes'; /eng'ke/ [ang'ko] 'is not'". Transcribed stress placements in the same excerpt: final in /ba'dur/ 'to sit down' (p. 132), /u'lun/ 'person' (p. 133), /a'puy/ 'fire' (p. 134), /u'tek/ 'brain' (p. 135), /semun'tuk/ 'be hitting' (p. 134); penultimate in /'walu/ 'eight' (p. 133), /'subu/ 'morning' (p. 135), /'loti/ 'be understanding', /ke'lati/ 'understood', /le'moti/ 'able to understand' (p. 135). (scanned renders schwa as 'a' or 'A'; segmental symbols normalised here, stress marks as printed.)
sources.locator: Moody, sec. 1 Introduction, two paragraphs, printed p. 131 top) + the volume cover; it contains NO st
sources.note: Only other phonological description of the language (per Goudswaard's own literature review, sec. 1.1.5), and it covers the Ida'an dialect proper whereas the held grammar describes the Begak dialect; would give an independent second statement on word stress for the dialect the record is named after. Low stakes: Goudswaard already states final stress for 'the Ida'an language' as a whole.

sources.note: Discourse paper (kat/koy particles, pivot marking, tense/aspect, sentence introducers). A full-text search of the extracted text conversion finds no occurrence of stress, accent, tone, penult, syllable, prosody, intonation or pitch. The only phonological remarks are morphophonemic (past -i- and -u- affixes coalescing with /a/ to ei/o, pp. 142-143). References list 'MOODY, David C., n.d., Ida'an phonemics. Unpublished manuscript.' (p. 162), cited on pp. 142-143 for the vowel coalescence, which is the author's phonology source and a lead for a stress statement.
